beats.intro: Chapter one. [[sub]]Money has time value: a dollar today is worth more than a dollar later. This chapter shows how to measure that.
beats.rate: [[chip1]]Would you rather have one hundred dollars today, or one hundred five in a year? [[arrow]]To give up today's money, most people want something extra. That extra, five percent, is the interest rate. [[l1]]For an investor, it is a required rate of return. [[l2]]Used to bring future money back to today, it is a discount rate. [[l3]]And it is the opportunity cost of spending now instead of investing.
beats.premiums: [[a]]An interest rate is more than one number. It is built in layers. [[l1]]At the bottom, the real risk-free rate: the pure reward for waiting. [[l2]]Add an inflation premium, to protect buying power. [[l3]]A default risk premium, for the chance the borrower does not pay. [[l4]]A liquidity premium, if the investment is hard to sell quickly. [[l5]]And a maturity premium, for the extra risk of a longer lending period. [[sum]]Together, they make the required rate.
beats.fv: Money you invest today grows. [[formula]]Future value equals present value, times one plus the rate, raised to the number of periods. [[bars]]Put one thousand dollars in at five percent. Each year the balance is multiplied by one point oh five. [[interest]]The green part is interest, and it keeps stacking up. [[year5]]After five years, you have twelve seventy-six twenty-eight. [[simple]]Simple interest would give only twelve fifty. The extra twenty-six twenty-eight is interest earned on interest.
beats.q1: Quick check. Find the future value.
beats.compounding: [[head]]Interest does not have to be paid once a year. A stated rate of six percent can be compounded more often. [[formula]]The effective annual rate is one plus the stated rate divided by m, to the power m, minus one. [[bars]]Annual compounding gives exactly six percent. Twice a year, six point oh nine. Quarterly, six point one three six. Monthly, six point one six eight. Daily, six point one eight three. [[cont]]And in the limit, continuous compounding, six point one eight four. [[note]]More frequent compounding always earns a little more, but the gains shrink quickly.
beats.q2: Quick check. Find the effective annual rate.
beats.pv: Present value runs the movie backwards. [[fv]]Twelve ten is due in two years, with a ten percent rate. [[back1]]Divide by one point one, and it is worth eleven hundred a year earlier. [[back2]]Divide again, and today it is worth one thousand. [[formula]]So present value is future value times one plus the rate, to the power of minus N. [[note]]A higher rate, or a longer wait, makes the present value smaller.
beats.q3: Quick check. Find the present value.
beats.annuity: Now a series. [[pay]]An ordinary annuity pays the same amount at the end of each period. Here, one thousand dollars at the end of each of three years, with a ten percent rate. [[d1]]Discount the first payment one year: nine hundred nine dollars and nine cents. [[d2]]The second, two years: eight twenty-six forty-five. [[d3]]The third, three years: seven fifty-one thirty-one. [[sum]]Add them up. The annuity is worth two thousand, four hundred eighty-six dollars and eighty-five cents today.
beats.perp: [[intro]]A perpetuity pays the same amount every period, forever. [[tank]]Watch what each payment is worth today. The first is worth about ninety-five dollars. Each later one is worth a little less. After ten payments, we have about seven seventy-two. After a hundred, nearly two thousand. [[formula]]The total never passes a limit. It is the payment divided by the rate: one hundred divided by five percent, two thousand dollars.
beats.solve: [[l1]]Often the rate is what is missing. Say one thousand dollars grows to fourteen forty in two years. Start with the future value formula. [[l2]]Fill in the numbers. [[l3]]Divide by one thousand. [[l4]]Take the square root. [[l5]]Subtract one. The rate is twenty percent. [[rule]]In general, the rate is the future over present value, to the power one over N, minus one.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]An interest rate is a required return, a discount rate, and an opportunity cost. [[w2]]Future value grows by one plus the rate every period, and interest earns interest. [[w3]]More frequent compounding raises the effective annual rate. [[w4]]Present value discounts. An annuity is a sum of present values, and a perpetuity is worth the payment divided by the rate. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
